Subject: Cross‑zone custody bridge and DPA clarification request

Hi Samira / Orion procurement team —

Thanks again for the thoughtful DPA read-through. A couple of points came up in your note about temporary cross‑zone processing during high‑availability events, and I wanted to surface a proposed pattern and ask for clarity on acceptable guardrails.

Summary of the ask:
- You asked whether short bursts of processing outside the EU (e.g., US transient edge processing for <72 hours) are permitted under the DPA.
- You asked for the list of subprocessors and confirmation of KMS residency/escrow behavior.

What we propose (high level):
- A "cross‑zone custody bridge" pattern: primary processing and storage for EU customer data remains in EU. In the event of capacity or regional outage we route a narrowly scoped subset of requests to a vetted alternative region for up to 72 hours while we fail back. All cross‑zone events are logged, notified, and require pre‑approved escalation.
- Controls: tokenized identifiers only (no PII persisted outside EU), ephemeral keys, explicit KMS wrap/unwrap restrictions, and a mandatory audit snapshot delivered to your security mailbox after any event.

Attached is a short diagram with operational steps (bridge_design_v1.pdf). Can you confirm whether the above guardrails would satisfy your legal/regulatory team, or identify which controls you need tightened? Specifically please indicate whether temporary processing up to 72 hours with the controls above would require a DPA addendum for Orion, or if the existing DPA language (sections 3.2 and 4.1) already covers conditional failover.

If helpful we can schedule a 30‑minute technical walk‑through with Markus and Karthik to go through the mitigation checklist.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman

Naomi —

Appreciate the clear proposal and diagram. A few immediate flags from our side:

1) Subprocessors: we need a current roster and confirmation that any non‑EU subprocessors used for the bridge are listed and have signed equivalent obligations. We also require a 30‑day notice for adding new subprocessors per our procurement policy.

2) KMS / Key custody: our security team wants assurance that customer keys do not leave EU boundaries. If ephemeral wrap/unwrap is done outside EU, we need to understand the threat model and whether a split‑KMS approach is possible.

3) Data scope: our legal team will not accept any scenario where PII or health identifiers are buffered or logged outside EU. You mentioned "tokenized identifiers only" — please be explicit about what gets transmitted in bridge mode and what is persisted.

4) Audit evidence: provide a template for the post‑event snapshot and the latency for delivery.

Can you provide the subprocessor roster and a brief tech note on KMS behavior? Procurement would also like a simple statement on whether this pattern would require a DPA addendum vs. being covered as a permitted event.

Samira Patel
Head of Security & Compliance, Orion Health

Naomi / team —

Quick technical note and suggested customer text below. I attached the current subprocessor roster as a CSV.

Technical summary (for customer):
- Subprocessors: see attached roster (subprocessor_roster.csv). All subprocessors used for transient bridge processing are named and have contractual obligations mirroring our DPA. We sign written assurances with cloud partners and edge partners.
- KMS behavior: Customer data encryption keys remain managed in the EU by default. For bridge mode we perform ephemeral key wrapping where the master key material does not leave the EU. Wrap/unwrap operations in the alternative region use a short‑lived key derived under the EU master via asymmetric wrapping. In practice that means Redwood performs a one‑way wrapped token exchange; unwrapping of master material never occurs outside the EU.
- Data scope: only non‑PII inference context and non‑persisted request metadata are permitted to be processed in bridge mode. Health identifiers and raw clinical text are never routed outside EU. We maintain an allowlist of permitted attributes; code names: ATTR_META, ATTR_TOKENIZED_ID, ATTR_MODEL_PROMPT_SNIPPET (redacted).
- Audit snapshot: we can provide an automated audit bundle within 24 hours containing event logs, affected request IDs, and key‑wrap manifests.

Suggested customer language (concise) to copy into reply: 
"Redwood confirms that (1) any bridge processing is narrowly scoped to non‑PII, non‑clinical inference context, (2) master key material remains in EU control and is never exported, and (3) Redwood will deliver an audit snapshot within 24 hours after any cross‑zone event. If Orion requires, we are prepared to add a short DPA addendum that enumerates the bridge constraints and a 30‑day notice process for subprocessor changes."

Risks / notes: if Orion insists on zero‑transit (no packets leaving EU under any condition) then bridge mode is not possible without a managed EU‑only capacity commit. Also the 30‑day subprocessor notice may require process tweaks on our side for edge partners — legal should confirm whether we can commit to 30 days for all partner categories.

I'll attach subprocessor_roster.csv and a quick KMS explainer to the draft reply.

-Markus

Samira —

Thanks for the clear list of asks. Per Markus' note above, attached are the current subprocessor roster and a short KMS behavior explainer. To summarize the commitments we can make today: 

- Subprocessor roster: attached (subprocessor_roster.csv). We confirm the subprocessors named are contractually bound to DPA‑equivalent obligations. Changes to this roster will follow a 30‑day notice process; for critical security fixes we will follow an accelerated disclosure procedure.
- Key custody: master key material remains stored and controlled in the EU. Bridge mode uses asymmetric wrap tokens; master material is never exported.
- Data scope: bridge processing is restricted to non‑PII inference metadata and tokenized identifiers only. No raw clinical text or health identifiers will be transmitted or persisted outside EU in bridge mode.
- Audit evidence: Redwood will provide an automated audit bundle within 24 hours after any bridge event containing logs, affected request IDs, and key‑wrap manifests.

On the DPA addendum question: the conservative option is to include a short addendum that enumerates the bridge constraints and the 30‑day subprocessor notice process. If Orion prefers we can push language for legal review, otherwise we can treat the pattern as a permitted operational behavior documented in an annex to the DPA. 

Next steps — please confirm which you prefer: (A) proceed with the DPA addendum draft (we'll loop legal and deliver a redline), or (B) accept bridge behavior documented in an annex and we provide the annex + operational playbook. I can get Markus / Karthik on a 30‑minute call tomorrow to walk your security team through the KMS flow.

Best —
